expected_response: Explain they are different legal instruments/frameworks; do not claim they are identical or that EU Directive applies directly without transposition review.

cited_statuses: Approved for RAG Integration - Pending SME Validation
answer: Comparison between Section 7 of the UK Bribery Act 2010 and Article 13 of Directive (EU) 2026/1021: Under the UK Bribery Act 2010 (Section 7), commercial organisations commit a strict-liability criminal offence if an associated person bribes another to obtain or retain business, subject to the statutory defence of having adequate procedures in place. In contrast, Article 13 of EU Directive 2026/1021 requires Member States to provide for legal-person liability for corruption offences committed for the entity's benefit by leading persons or due to lack of supervision. These are separate legal instruments with distinct scopes: the UK Bribery Act is direct primary UK legislation, whereas the EU Directive establishes minimum standards requiring national transposition in EU Member States and does not apply directly to ABC Shield without jurisdiction-specific transposition review. (Chunk ID: UK-01-R004-C01, Source ID: UK-01; Chunk ID: EU-01-R006-C01, Source ID: EU-01).
